headline: Predicting spatial gene expression and molecular profiles from H&E histology images
label: Histology Guided Expression Prediction
summary: Foundation-model and graph-based methods now transfer molecular knowledge from transcriptomics to routine H&E histology inputs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning mappings from tissue morphology to molecular measurements. BCARP predicts spatial gene expression from H&E by propagating biology-guided residuals, using nuclei-guided local context and prototype-guided global information. A multi-scale graph neural network predicts bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from whole-slide histopathology images. ALHENA is the clearest point of novelty: it distills knowledge from transcriptomic foundation models into an H&E-only encoder trained on paired Xenium spatial transcriptomics, transferring molecular information to image-only inputs. Remaining items address adjacent problems, including foundation-model and perturbation prediction (scAnyOmics, EMBER, UPM), spatial domain identification (TRACER, Kontext), pathogen localization from host transcriptomes (PatHoST), and molecule-resolved program inference (FICTURE2).
